To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Ao Tien, Vietnam, experienced increased effective moisture during the Little Ice age, with the greatest wetness occurring during the 18th Century.
1) Ao Tien is a new proxy record of climate in northern Vietnam that provides a 650- yr record of effective moisture.

(i) Ao Tien records a significant increase in effective moisture during ~1400–1850 CE; (ii) the Ao Tien hydroclimate record is significantly correlated with a reconstructed Southern Oscillation index of precipitation, which suggests that the Little Ice Age was characterized by a prolonged La Niña-like state; (iii) the Ao Tian record exhibits a drying signal during the last ~30 years that is consistent with the weakening of the Walker circulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reconstruction of hydroclimate in northern Vietnam over the last 650 years.
the hydroclimatology of northern Vietnam over the last 650 years and its relationship to large-scale climate patterns.
a 650-year record of effective moisture in northernmost Vietnam.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Pacific Walker circulation was the dominant control of hydroclimate variability in Vietnam and the Southeast Asian region during the past 600 years.
a prolonged La Niña-like state was present during the Little Ice age, which was responsible for the overall wetter conditions, but this does not preclude the possibility of regional variability.
a wetter Little Ice Age in northern Vietnam occurred due to a persistent La Nina-like state, which is consistent with a robust tree-rings hydroclimate reconstruction from Vietnam.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ao Tien δ18O record is consistent with the idea that the Little Ice Age was wet in northern Vietnam.
a prolonged La Niña-like state prevailed in northern Vietnam during much of the Little Ice Age (i.e., ~1400-1750 CE), which is consistent with other regional hydroclimate records from Southeast Asia.
the Little Ice Age in northern Vietnam was a time of overall wetter conditions, punctuated with significant droughts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Little Ice Age was a wet period in Vietnam, and that a significant drying trend has occurred over the last 150 years.

the Ao Tien site is sensitive to the large-scale hydroclimate of Vietnam and that the hydroclimate of the Little Ice Age was wetter than the last 30 years, which has important implications for the region's water resources.
